submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker records status=UNDER_CONSTRUCTION, expectedOpening=2026-06-30 (unqualified). Source says the project's Port KC bond application was withdrawn (~June 2026, exact date approximate — this session could not WebFetch the article to confirm) after utility Evergy could not deliver full power supply by the planned June 1, 2026 energization date (full supply not expected until late summer 2026); separately, Missouri Independent (2026-06-12) reports the project's partners are in arbitration over alleged cost overruns, delays, and financing/management failures. submissions.title: Le préfet de Seine-et-Marne a validé le projet Campus IA de Fouju (1,4 GW et 50 milliards €)
submissions.excerpt: Le préfet de Seine-et-Marne a validé le projet Campus IA de Fouju
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker status=PERMITTING (public inquiry pending). Source says: by decree n° 2026-07/DCSE/BPE/E dated 2026-07-29, the prefect of Seine-et-Marne formally authorized the Campus IA project (Campus AI + RTE) following the inquiry commission's favorable report (early July 2026). First-phase construction is now scheduled to start September 2026, service entry targeted 2028, later phases 2030-2033 and 2034-2038. Recommend moving status off PERMITTING now that the decision has been published. Primary corroboration: Préfecture de Seine-et-Marne decisions page, https://www.seine-et-marne.gouv.fr/Publications/Enquetes-publiques/FOUJU-PROJET-CAMPUS-IA/DECISIONS (WebFetch to both seine-et-marne.gouv.fr and dcmag.fr was blocked this session; corroborated via WebSearch snippets citing both, plus next.ink). Note a coalition of environmental associations has announced legal proceedings against the authorization, so 'approved' does not mean litigation risk is closed — worth a caveat in the note field.

submissions.title: Merlin espera la licencia para arrancar su mayor centro de datos de 1,4 GW
submissions.excerpt: su mayor centro de datos de 1,4 GW
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker records status=ANNOUNCED, estimatedMw=2000 (both campuses combined), capex=null, expectedOpening=null, 'no construction, tenant, capex or timeline confirmed.' Source says the Navalmoral de la Mata sub-site ALONE is now designed for up to 1.4GW IT capacity (initial 200MW phase + later 1.2GW expansion) — Merlin CEO Ismael Clemente says construction on the first 20MW/€400M phase could start end-September 2026 pending a building license, with operation ~2.5 years after construction starts (~early 2029). Corroborating: Cope.es 2026-06-22 (https://www.cope.es/emisoras/extremadura/caceres-provincia/caceres/noticias/merlin-pone-fecha-centro-datos-navalmoral-obras-arrancar-septiembre-20260622_3388748.html) and El Economista 2026-06 (https://www.eleconomista.es/energia/noticias/13981368/06/26/el-centro-de-datos-de-navalmoral-estaria-en-funcionamiento-en-dos-anos-y-medio-si-las-obras-arrancan-en-septiembre.html). Also, Junta de Extremadura published Navalmoral's integrated environmental authorization application for public consultation on 2026-05-22 (govt filing) — real permitting activity, not pure pre-announcement. Valdecaballeros (the second campus) shows no comparable update, still aspirational. Recommend splitting the combined row's basis or adding a Navalmoral-specific capex/timeline; do not simply raise the combined estimatedMw without checking whether Valdecaballeros is still ~1GW or also revised. WebFetch to all cited Spanish outlets was blocked this session; corroborated via WebSearch across 3+ independent Spanish outlets.

claims.methodology: Navalmoral de la Mata sub-site alone (one of the two Edged-Merlin Extremadura campuses) now reported at up to 1.4GW IT capacity design (200MW initial + 1.2GW expansion), per Spanish trade press citing Merlin. This is a single-site figure, not the combined-campus total. Still a design target pending construction license — not confirmed/operating.

submissions.title: Oracle to deploy up to 2.45GW of Bloom fuel cells at New Mexico data center
submissions.excerpt: Oracle to deploy up to 2.45GW of Bloom fuel cells at New Mexico data center
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker deliberately leaves power blank for this site ('no per-site capacity was published, so power is left blank rather than guessed') — that remains CORRECT for IT load, which is still genuinely undisclosed; do not fill IT load from this source. But a GENERATION-capacity figure now exists and is missing from the record: Oracle/BorderPlex/Bloom Energy announced 2026-04-27 (primary source: https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/oracle-borderplex-and-bloom-energy-to-power-project-jupiter-with-fuel-cell-technology-2026-04-27/) that up to 2.45GW of Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells will be the site's sole power source, operating as a single behind-the-meter microgrid, replacing a prior gas-turbine plan. Recommend recording this explicitly as a GENERATION-basis metric, clearly labeled and separate from IT load, specifically to avoid the site-power-vs-IT-load conflation this audit targets — 2.45GW must never become this project's headline 'power' figure without the generation caveat attached. WebFetch to oracle.com and datacenterdynamics.com was blocked this session; corroborated via WebSearch across DCD, American Public Power Association, and Oracle's own newsroom URL/title.

claims.methodology: Oracle/BorderPlex/Bloom Energy's own April 2026 announcement: up to 2.45GW of Bloom fuel-cell GENERATION capacity (behind-the-meter microgrid) for the whole Project Jupiter campus, replacing a prior gas-turbine plan. Explicitly NOT an IT-load figure — IT load remains undisclosed. Primary-source text not directly fetched this session (network-blocked), hence MEDIUM not HIGH despite being a company announcement per underlying reporting.
